basis_ref: DESIGN.md §The join graph (child ParentProcessId → parent TargetProcessId: process tree lineage); CrowdStrike data model, not corpus-validated (DESIGN.md §What still genuinely needs a real corpus)
note: A child process's ParentProcessId equals the parent's TargetProcessId. This is the process-tree edge.

basis_ref: DESIGN.md §The join graph (event ContextProcessId → process TargetProcessId: which process caused this event); CrowdStrike data model, not corpus-validated (public corpus samples ContextProcessId as 000000000000)
target_label: the process that caused this event
note: On a non-process event (DnsRequest, file, registry...), ContextProcessId identifies the process that caused it. This is how you attribute activity to a process.

basis_ref: DESIGN.md §The join graph (TreeId groups a whole detection/activity tree); FDR_REFERENCE.md §3 (TreeId: process-tree correlation ID)
target_label: every event in the same activity tree
note: Groups an entire related activity/detection tree.

basis_ref: DESIGN.md §The join graph (RawProcessId: the OS-visible PID; not unique over time, unsafe as a join key alone); curated/translations.json evidence (28 paired documents: no arithmetic converts RawProcessId to TargetProcessId)
target_label: TargetProcessId candidates on ProcessRollup2 / SyntheticProcessRollup2 for this OS PID (a lookup, never a direct join)
note: The OS-visible PID. NOT unique over time -- PIDs are recycled. Never join on this alone; always scope by aid AND a time window.

hazard.text: RawProcessId is the OS PID and is recycled: without aid AND a tight time window this matches unrelated processes. Expect multiple rows; disambiguate on ImageFileName and ProcessStartTime, then carry TargetProcessId forward.

basis_ref: cim/fdr_to_cim_fields.csv row 1: TA appinfo LOOKUP keyed on SHA256HashData on crowdstrike:events:external (the TA treats the detection-event hash as the same value space); kb/enrichment SHA256String join_candidates → SHA256HashData (confidence medium)

note: SHA256String on a detection summary event is the same SHA256 value space as SHA256HashData on sensor telemetry; pivot on the hash to find every process and file event that touched the file.
